chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Talib, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man from the Ansar said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Who is the most deserving of filial piety?' He said: 'Your parents.' He said: 'They have passed away.' He said: 'Be pious to your children.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the most deserving of filial piety after parents die?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the continuity of *birr* (filial piety) by shifting the focus from deceased parents to their offspring, establishing a chain of virtue that persists beyond death. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining familial bonds (*silat al-rahim*) as a means of honoring the deceased, a concept deeply rooted in the broader Islamic ethic of kindness to kin.
